title: Sail
description:
### Sail (experimental)

- Adds experimental support for [Sail](https://github.com/lakehq/sail), a
Spark Connect server written in Rust that needs no JVM. Use
`spark_connect(method = "sail")`:
  - With `master = "local"`, it starts a Sail server inside the R session, on
  a free port. `spark_disconnect()` stops the server, and so does ending the R
  session.
  - With a `master` such as `"sc://localhost:50051"`, it connects to a Sail
  server that is already running. That server's Python environment needs
  `pyspark-client`, and for `spark_apply()`, also `rpy2`, R, and the same
  Python version as the R session.

- Adds `install_sail()`. It creates a Python environment with `pysail`, the
`pyspark-client` version that `pysail` pins, and `rpy2`. Its `version` is the
Sail version, for example `"0.7"`.

- `spark_apply()` works with Sail. With a local server, the R code in the
function runs inside the user's R session, on Sail's threads, instead of in a
separate process. This means a crash in the function can end the R session, and
the function can change the session's global environment.

- Sail does not support caching. `copy_to()` and `spark_read_*()` need
`memory = FALSE`, and `compute()` returns an error.

- The ML functions and `tune_grid_spark()` are not supported with Sail.

- Adds a CI workflow that runs the tests against Sail. Set the `SAIL_VERSION`
environment variable to run the tests against Sail locally.

- Internally, `pysparklyr` now keeps the back-end version, which names the
Python environment, separate from the Python library version. They are the
same number for every back-end except Sail.

### Other changes

- `copy_to(memory = FALSE)` now creates the table under its name, so
`tbl(sc, name)` finds it. Before, it created a table with a random name. It
also returns an error if the table exists, unless `overwrite = TRUE`. This does
not apply to Snowflake yet.

- Connection errors for back-ends other than Databricks no longer show a
Databricks error message.

title: Fully delegate Databricks auth to the SDK and add Connect support
description:
Previously we had custom R-side auth resolution that largely duplicated what the Databricks Python SDK already handles natively, but didn't include newer methods (e.g. workload identity).

This commit delegates all auth to the SDK's unified authentication flow, giving us PATs, CLI OAuth, profiles, Workbench tokens, M2M OAuth, and workload identity for free. The only auth requiring R-side code is Posit Connect credentials (viewer and service account tokens, which we get via connectcreds).

Unit tests are included.

Closes #182.

title: Updates
description:
- Fixed #185: restored `tbl_pyspark` connection recovery under sparklyr 1.9.5 / dbplyr 2.6.0 by adding `spark_connection.tbl_pyspark()` and stashing the full connection where `remote_con()` reads it.  
- Fixed `left_join()` (and other two-table verbs) failing with "`x` and `y` must share the same source" by adding `same_src.tbl_pyspark()` that compares the stable `connection_id`.
- Replaced the deprecated `dbplyr::as.sql()` call with `as_table_path()` to remove the dbplyr 2.6.0 deprecation warning.
- Stopped the spurious reticulate "After Python has initialized…" warnings by only calling `py_require()` before Python initializes.
- Fixed the 6 user-agent test failures by unsetting `SPARK_CONNECT_USER_AGENT` within the affected tests.
- Added a regression test for #185 and updated the dplyr snapshots for the new dbplyr output format.
- Bumped the dev version to `0.2.1.9000`, updated NEWS, and raised minimums to `sparklyr (>= 1.9.5)` and `dbplyr (>= 2.6.0)`.
- Removed the `sparklyr/sparklyr` remote

title: Fully delegate Snowflake auth to the SDK and add Connect support
description:
Previously we had special handling for a couple of different authenticators but didn't natively support the default connection behaviour of the Snowflake SDKs (and `odbc::snowflake()`). This commit delegates all of the auth handling to the Python SDK, giving us all supported authenticators for free.

The only auth method requiring specific R-side code is viewer credentials on Posit Connect, which we now get via `connectcreds` (like we do for Databricks already).

Unit tests are included.

title: Fix collect() failure when pandas columns contain NULL values, date type mapping and tune-grid pipe placeholder compatibility
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes three issues in Spark → Pandas → R collection.

---

### 1) NULL columns broke tibble conversion

**Before**

Collecting tables with NULL-heavy columns failed:

```r
sparklyr::sdf_sql(sc, "SELECT * FROM "...") %>% head()
```

Error:

```
Error in `dplyr::as_tibble()`:
! All columns in a tibble must be vectors.
✖ Column `X` is NULL.
✖ Column `Y` is NULL.
...
```

**Fix**

`to_pandas_cleaned()` now flattens fallback output into proper R vectors while preserving row count, preventing literal `NULL` columns.

**After**

`head()` collects successfully without tibble errors.

---

### 2) Spark `date` returned as `<dbl>`

**Before**

Date columns sometimes arrived as numeric (days since epoch):

```r
sparklyr::sdf_sql(sc, "...") %>% select(modification_date)
```

```
modification_date
<dbl>
17680
17301
...
```

**Fix**

If `py_type == "date"`, values are explicitly converted via:

```r
as.Date(x, origin = "1970-01-01")
```

across degraded R-side types (`numeric`, `integer`, `character`, `list`, `logical`).

**After**

```
modification_date
<date>
2018-05-29
2017-05-15
...
```

---

### 3) `tune-grid.R` pipe placeholder parse error

**Before**

```r
... |> _$val
```

Could fail with:

```
pipe placeholder can only be used as a named argument
```

**Fix**

Replaced with parser-safe equivalent:

```r
... |> (\(x) x$val)()
```

Behavior unchanged; compatibility improved.

title: Adds support for R UDFs
description:
Builds the foundation that allows R functions to run in Spark/Databricks Connect
- It uses the `rpy2` Python library to serialize and run the R code inside the cluster
- It uses `applyInPandas()` to run the R function (via `rpy2`) against a grouped data frame
- It uses `mapInPandas()` to run the R function (via `rpy2`) against non-grouped data frames
- Properly sets the max Arrow batch to partition de data
- Wraps functionality into `spark_apply()`. Most of the integration is in functions that `spark_apply()` calls, so the functionality can be re-used by future interfaces
- Adds `rpy2` to the list of packages to be installed by `install_databricks()`/`install_pyspark()`
- Verifies if `rpy2` is not install in your current Python environment and offers to install
- Adds tests

description:
- Switches form using the Pyspark function of `listCatalogs`/`listDatabases`/`listTables` to a SQL based approach using `SHOW CATALOG/DATABASES/TABLES`. 
- This allows us to specify the Catalog to pull when requesting a list of Databases, which is not possible with the Pyspark function
- We also avoid setting the Catalog and Database via `setCurrentCatalog`, and `setCurrentDatabase` which appear to be very expensive operations, processing-wise
- It stops loading default tables at the root of the structure. This seems to be the biggest gain in rendering time

title: use virtualenv instead of venv on databricks
description:
The databricks environment doesn't install the apt package `python3-venv`, and the python module `venv` that reticulate discovers under the system python is not usable. 

The image however does contain an installation of `virtualenv` under `/usr/local`, which we can point reticulate at.
